question: Is a sorted register-weight-stationary MoE expert path worth shipping over channel-major-L2, at the batched-decode target B={4,8}?
method: Monte-Carlo random top-k routing, k=8 distinct experts/token, E=128, 20000 trials/point; group = slots routed to same expert.

verdict.reason: avg group 1.10/1.24 at B=4/8; HBM-read save ceiling 9%/19.3%, already captured by channel-major-L2 (co-routed slots adjacent -> reuse distance ~1 expert row << L2). Sort recovers only the L2-missed slice, at the cost of an align/sort packet on the decode critical path + MM-accumulator registers in an already register-bound (219 reg, 1 block/SM) megakernel — the exact op74 p9-batch implemented and measured-rejected.
verdict.crossover_note: grouping profitable (36-56% ceiling) at B>=16 IF register pressure solved (e.g. separate non-megakernel expert launch).

measured_tpot_scaling_context.implication: TPOT scales far below distinct-expert-traffic ratio -> expert-weight streaming is a minority of decode cost (shared q/k/v/o/lm_head GEMVs + fixed attention/router/sampling dominate); perfecting the <=19% expert-collision slice is a low-single-digit end-to-end lever at B<=8.
